intro: Here in Antalya province lies Olympos, an ancient city of the 2nd century BC. Its ruins are wrapped in laurel forest, beside the never-dying flames of Chimaera.
history: Olympos was once notorious as a pirate base, and it was pacified only when Rome cleared the seas. Around the natural gas flames nearby, the cult of Hephaestus grew — a cult born beside a fire that never goes out.
structure-5: You are now at the Chimaera flames, everlasting flames rising from the rock. In myth they are the breath of the Chimera. Pause for a moment and watch them burn.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the harbour baths and the theatre, then the sarcophagi, and finally the bridge piers.
facts: Did you know? The flames of Chimaera have burned without pause for at least 2,500 years. In the first century BC the pirate chief Zeniketes made the city his base, and Rome had to drive him out. Today the ruins are swallowed by laurel and oleander, with a stream running through the middle of the city to the sea.
outro: This brings our journey through Olympos to an end. Please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. The flames have burned here for so long; let the ruins rest just as long. Enjoy your visit.
